title: Linear Equations
tagline: Year 2 — One and two variables, word problems and consistency

introduction.overview: A linear equation has variables only to the first power. One equation in one variable, like 3x + 5 = 20, is solved by isolating x. Two equations in two variables, like x + y = 10 and x − y = 2, are solved by substitution or elimination. Many word problems (ages, money, digits, shares) become linear equations once you name the unknowns.
introduction.placementRelevance: Linear equations are commonly asked in company aptitude rounds, directly and as the engine of age, digit and money problems.
introduction.realWorldContext: Budget splits, break-even calculations, mixture quantities and speed-time relations are solved with linear equations.

learningObjectives: Solve linear equations in one variable
Solve two equations in two variables by elimination and substitution
Solve digit, age, money and fraction problems
Decide whether a pair of equations has one, no or infinitely many solutions

prerequisiteKnowledge.quickRefresher: Whatever you do to one side of an equation, do to the other. A pair of equations with two unknowns needs two independent equations.

coreDefinitions: Linear equation: ax + b = 0 form, variables to the power 1.
Solution: values that make the equation true.
Elimination: add or subtract the equations to remove one variable.
Substitution: express one variable in terms of the other and substitute.
Consistency: a pair a₁x + b₁y = c₁, a₂x + b₂y = c₂ has a unique solution if a₁/a₂ ≠ b₁/b₂, no solution if a₁/a₂ = b₁/b₂ ≠ c₁/c₂, infinitely many if all three ratios are equal.
conceptExplanation.theoreticalIntuition: An equation is a balance. Operations that keep the balance (adding the same number, multiplying both sides) do not change the solution. Two unknowns need two balances, and combining them removes one unknown.
conceptExplanation.visualOrMentalModel: In a word problem, define the unknown for exactly what is asked, write each sentence as an equation, and solve. Check by substituting back into the story.

importantRulesAndFormulas.title: Elimination
importantRulesAndFormulas.formula: Multiply to match coefficients, then add or subtract

importantRulesAndFormulas.title: Cramer-type shortcut
importantRulesAndFormulas.formula: x = (c₁b₂ − c₂b₁)/(a₁b₂ − a₂b₁), y = (a₁c₂ − a₂c₁)/(a₁b₂ − a₂b₁)

importantRulesAndFormulas.title: Consistency
importantRulesAndFormulas.whenToUse: Value of k for identical lines.

mainNarrative: For one variable, move terms so x is alone. 3x + 5 = 20 gives 3x = 15 and x = 5. For fractions, multiply by the LCM: (x + 1)/2 − (x − 1)/3 = 3 becomes 3(x + 1) − 2(x − 1) = 18, so x + 5 = 18 and x = 13.

For two variables, use elimination. From 3x + 2y = 16 and x + y = 6, double the second to get 2x + 2y = 12, then subtract: x = 4 and y = 2. Substitution gives the same result: y = 6 − x, so 3x + 12 − 2x = 16.

Word problems: name the unknowns. Three pens and two pencils cost ₹34; two pens and three pencils cost ₹31. With pen = p and pencil = q: 3p + 2q = 34 and 2p + 3q = 31. Eliminate q: 9p + 6q = 102 and 4p + 6q = 62, so 5p = 40 and p = 8, q = 5.

Digit problems: let the digits be a and b. If the digits add to 9 and reversing them increases the number by 27, then (10b + a) − (10a + b) = 9(b − a) = 27, so b − a = 3. With a + b = 9 the digits are 3 and 6, and the number is 36.
Consistency: the equations 2x + 3y = 5 and 4x + ky = 10 describe the same line when the ratios of all coefficients are equal: 2/4 = 3/k = 5/10, so k = 6.

deepDiveAspects.title: Substitute to check
deepDiveAspects.content: After solving, substitute the values back into both equations and, for word problems, into the story. This catches mistakes in translation.

deepDiveAspects.title: Number of unknowns and equations
deepDiveAspects.content: With fewer equations than unknowns you get a family of solutions; the question will then give integer or range conditions that fix the answer.

solvedExamples.title: Pens and pencils
solvedExamples.question: 3 pens and 2 pencils cost ₹34 and 2 pens and 3 pencils cost ₹31. Find the price of a pen.

solvedExamples.title: Two-digit number
solvedExamples.question: The sum of the digits of a two-digit number is 9. If the digits are reversed, the number increases by 27. Find the number.

steps.title: Solve
steps.explanation: a + b = 9 and b − a = 3 give b = 6, a = 3.

solvedExamples.commonTrap: Mixing the tens and units digits.

shortcutMethods.title: Elimination first

traditionalVsShortcut.shortcutMethod: Multiply to match one coefficient, add or subtract, and solve; or use the Cramer formula for awkward numbers.

rulesForApplication: Define unknowns for what is asked.

commonMistakes.whyItHappens: Writing "3 less than x" as 3 − x.

placementTips.eliminationTechnique: Test the options in the original equations; only one satisfies both.
placementTips.recruiterInsight: Linear equations underlie ages, mixtures and speeds.

placementStyle.explanation: a − 4 = 3(b − 4) gives a = 3b − 8. a + 6 = 2(b + 6) gives 3b − 2 = 2b + 12, so b = 14 and a = 34.

placementStyle.explanation: Adding: 8x = 32, so x = 4. Then 12 + 4y = 24, so y = 3. x + y = 7.
